title: Learning the solution operator of parametric partial differential equations with physics-informed DeepONets
authors_full: Sifan Wang, Hanwen Wang, Paris Perdikaris
affiliations: University of Pennsylvania, Philadelphia, PA, USA - Sifan Wang and Hanwen Wang: Graduate Group in Applied Mathematics and Computational Science; Paris Perdikaris: Department of Mechanical Engineering and Applied Mechanics
identifier: DOI:10.1126/sciadv.abi8605 (analyzed PDF is arXiv:2103.10974v1 preprint, 19 Mar 2021)
subdomain: physics-informed operator learning for parametric PDEs: anti-derivative operator, 1D parametric ODE, diffusion-reaction, Burgers equation, Eikonal equation (signed distance functions of parametric circles and airfoils)
industry_context: General scientific ML for engineering design and control, Earth system science, computational biology (no named company/lab); funded by US DOE (DE-SC0019116, DE-AR0001201) and AFOSR (FA9550-20-1-0060); airfoil case uses UIUC Airfoil Data Site (aerospace context)
physics_enforced_exact: Four parametric benchmarks. (1) Anti-derivative operator (1D parametric ODE): ds(x)/dx = u(x), s(0)=0, x in [0,1]. (2) Nonlinear diffusion-reaction PDE with source term u(x): ds/dt = D*d2s/dx2 + k*s^2 + u(x), (x,t) in (0,1]x[0,1], D=0.01 (diffusion coefficient), k=0.01 (reaction rate), zero initial and boundary conditions. (3) 1D Burgers equation (benchmark of Li et al. [32]): ds/dt + s*ds/dx - nu*d2s/dx2 = 0, (x,t) in (0,1)x(0,1), s(x,0)=u(x), periodic BCs (s(0,t)=s(1,t), ds/dx(0,t)=ds/dx(1,t)), viscosity nu=0.01. (4) Eikonal equation ||grad s(x)||_2 = 1, s(x)=0 on the boundary (solution = signed distance function of a parametric closed curve Gamma: circles of varying radius or airfoil shapes)
pde_type: multiple (first-order ODE; parabolic diffusion-reaction; Burgers convection-diffusion; hyperbolic Eikonal/Hamilton-Jacobi)
nonlinearity: strongly nonlinear (Burgers convective term s*ds/dx, quadratic reaction k*s^2, Eikonal norm-of-gradient constraint; anti-derivative case linear)
bcs_ic_handled: All as soft penalties in the loss. Anti-derivative: s(0)=0 via |G_theta(u)(0)|^2 term. Diffusion-reaction: zero IC/BC via L_operator at P=100 points uniformly sampled on the boundary of [0,1]x[0,1] (excluding t=1). Burgers: IC s(x,0)=u(x) via L_IC (eq 4.16, P=100 points) and periodic BCs via L_BC (eqs 4.17-4.18: value and x-derivative matching at x=0 and x=1). Eikonal: s=0 on the boundary curve via L_BC at m sensor points on Gamma
enforcement_mechanism: soft-penalty on operator outputs - PDE residuals of the DeepONet prediction are added as L2 penalties to the composite loss; no hard-constraint or projection layer
enforcement_details: Automatic differentiation of the DeepONet output G_theta(u)(y) with respect to the trunk-net input coordinates y forms the PDE residual: diffusion-reaction R = dG/dt - D*d2G/dx2 - k*G^2 (eq 4.7), Burgers R = dG/dt + G*dG/dx - nu*d2G/dx2 (eq 4.14), Eikonal R = ||grad_y G||_2 (eq 4.23); residual minimized at Q collocation points per input function u^(i) via L_physics = 1/(NQm) * sum_{i,j,k} |N(u^(i)(x_k), G_theta(u^(i))(y_j))|^2 (eq 3.2); combined with L_operator (paired-data MSE or BC/IC penalties) into L = L_operator + L_physics (eq 3.1)
network_architecture: Unstacked DeepONet: separate branch and trunk fully-connected networks merged via dot product (eq 2.3; 100 basis functions in Fig 1). PI-DeepONet per benchmark (Table 6): anti-derivative, 1D ODE (regular and irregular), diffusion-reaction: 5 layers, 50 units/hidden layer; Burgers: 7 layers, 100 units; Eikonal circles: 6 layers, 50 units; Eikonal airfoils: 6 layers, 100 units. Irregular-input ODE: branch and trunk 5 layers/200 units with trunk input y embedded by random Fourier features gamma(y)=[cos(By); sin(By)], B~N(0,sigma^2), sigma=50. Burgers also tested with the modified MLP backbone of Wang et al. [57] (eqs G.1-G.6). Conventional DeepONet baselines (Table 7): e.g. 3-layer/100-unit (anti-derivative) and 5-layer/50-unit elsewhere
activation_function: tanh everywhere except Eikonal airfoils (ELU); ReLU tested on the pedagogical vanilla DeepONet (poor residual fit attributed to non-smooth activations)
input_representation: Branch net: input function u evaluated at m fixed sensors (m=100-250; equispaced grid or uniform random) -> [u(x1),...,u(xm)]; trunk net: query coordinates y=(x,t) or (x,y); Fourier-feature case: trunk input embedded via gamma(y)=[cos(By); sin(By)]; Eikonal: branch input is the parameterized boundary curve Gamma evaluated at m sensors (circle radius/angles or airfoil outline points)
output_representation: Scalar field prediction G_theta(u)(y) = sum_{k=1}^p b_k(u)*t_k(y): solution s(x,t) (ODE/PDE cases) or signed distance function s(x,y); outputs are differentiated w.r.t. y by autodiff to build the residuals
loss_terms: L(theta) = L_operator(theta) + L_physics(theta) (+ L_IC, L_BC where applicable), eq 3.1. L_operator = 1/(NP) sum |G_theta(u^(i))(y_j) - G(u^(i))(y_j)|^2 (eq 2.4; repurposed to enforce zero IC/BC when no paired data). L_physics = 1/(NQm) sum |N(u^(i)(x_k), G_theta(u^(i))(y_j))|^2 (eq 3.2). Anti-derivative physics-only (eq 4.4): 1/N sum |G_theta(u)(0)|^2 + 1/(NQ) sum |dG/dy|_{y=x_j} - u^(i)(x_j)|^2. Diffusion-reaction (eq 4.9): 1/(NP) sum |G_theta(u)(x_u,j, t_u,j)|^2 (zero IC/BC) + 1/(NQ) sum |R^(i)(x_j,t_j) - u^(i)(x_j)|^2. Burgers (eq 4.20): lambda*L_IC + L_BC + L_physics with L_physics = 1/(NQ) sum |R^(i)(x_j,t_j)|^2 (eq 4.19). Eikonal (eq 4.25): 1/(Nm) sum |G_theta(Gamma^(i))(x_j,y_j)|^2 + 1/(NQ) sum |R^(i)(x_j,y_j) - 1|^2
loss_weighting: Fixed (equal weights) in all cases except Burgers: L = lambda*L_IC + L_BC + L_physics with lambda in {1,5,10,20,50,100}; smallest average error 1.38e-02 at lambda=20 (Fig 11a); Appendix B: hyper-parameters tuned manually, not optimized
sampling_strategy: Input functions sampled from Gaussian random fields (exponential-quadratic kernel k_l(x1,x2)=exp(-||x1-x2||^2/2l^2), l=0.2 regular / l=0.01 irregular; Burgers ICs: N(0,25^2*(-Delta+5^2*I)^-4)); mini-batch training, batch size 10,000 default; m sensors equispaced (ODE cases) or uniform random; Q collocation points uniformly/randomly sampled per input function (Q=100-2,500, Table 5); Burgers IC/BC/residual points randomly sampled in the domain; Eikonal curve points uniformly sampled on Gamma
optimizer_schedule: Adam (default settings) with exponential learning-rate decay 0.9 every 1,000 iterations; no L-BFGS stage. Iterations (Table 5): anti-derivative 4e4; 1D ODE regular 4e4; 1D ODE irregular 3e5; diffusion-reaction 1.2e5; Burgers 2e5; Eikonal circles 8e4; airfoils 1.2e5
training_compute: Single NVIDIA V100 GPU. Training hours (Table 8): anti-derivative 0.15 (PI) vs 0.03 (DeepONet); 1D ODE regular 0.15 vs 0.03; 1D ODE irregular 1.61 (PI-MLP) / 1.37 (PI-Fourier-feature); diffusion-reaction 2.27 (PI) vs 1.13 (DeepONet); Burgers 7.61 (PI-MLP) / 9.25 (PI-modified-MLP); Eikonal circles 0.76; airfoils 0.38. PI training is slower than vanilla DeepONet because autodiff PDE residuals enlarge the computational graph
data_regime: Ranges from data-driven to fully physics-only. (a) Pedagogical anti-derivative: 10,000 paired (u,s) samples (P=1 output observation each; u from GP l=0.215, s via RK45), test 1,000 with P=100. (b) Physics-only 1D ODE: N=10,000 input functions u known exactly (GRF l=0.2, Q=m=100), no paired outputs of s except s(0)=0. (c) Irregular-input ODE: N=100,000 u-samples (l=0.01, Q=m=200), no paired outputs. (d) Diffusion-reaction: N=10,000 source terms from GRF l=0.2, no paired outputs (reference solutions via 2nd-order implicit finite difference on a 100x100 grid used only for testing; 1,000 test realizations). (e) Burgers: N=1,000 training initial-condition functions (from 2,000 sampled); spectral (Chebfun/ETDRK4, dt=0.01, 101 snapshots) solutions only for testing (1,000 realizations, 101x101 grid). (f) Eikonal circles: 1,000 circles (uniform radii), analytic SDF for testing; airfoils: 1,552 shapes from UIUC Airfoil Data Site, first 1,000 train / 552 test, no SDF observations
datasets_used: Anti-derivative operator (GRF l=0.2 and l=0.01); 1D parametric ODE; parametric diffusion-reaction system; 1D Burgers benchmark of Li et al. [32] (nu=0.01); Eikonal equation - parametric circles (analytic SDF) and parametric airfoils (UIUC Airfoil Data Site, 1,552 airfoil geometries)
baselines_compared: Conventional data-driven DeepONet [33] (ReLU and Tanh variants); Fourier neural operator of Li et al. [32] (qualitative comparison on Burgers: comparable accuracy although FNO is trained on a large corpus of paired input-output data); standard fully-connected vs Fourier feature network vs modified MLP [57] backbones; conventional spectral solver (Chebfun) for inference timing
evaluation_metrics: Relative L2 prediction error (mean +/- std over 1,000 test examples), relative L2 of the residual u (ODE cases), point-wise error, inference wall-clock time (sec) vs number of PDEs solved
key_quantitative_results: Anti-derivative with paired data (Table 1): PI-DeepONet (Tanh) rel-L2 of s = 2.49e-03 +/- 2.74e-03 vs DeepONet (ReLU) 5.16e-03 +/- 4.58e-03 and DeepONet (Tanh) 1.89e-01 +/- 1.51e-01 (residual u: 6.29e-03 vs 1.39e-01 / 6.14e-01). Physics-only with zero paired data (Table 2): rel-L2 of s = 3.25e-03 +/- 3.19e-03 (u: 6.97e-03 +/- 3.95e-03) vs vanilla DeepONet degenerate operator 8.80e-01 +/- 4.72e-01. Data efficiency: vanilla DeepONet needs >10x more training data for equal accuracy (Fig 4); diffusion-reaction: rel-L2 1.92% +/- 1.12% (DeepONet with 100 paired outputs per u) vs ~0.45% +/- 0.16% (PI-DeepONet, no paired outputs) - ~80% accuracy gain with 100% data reduction (Fig 9). Irregular inputs l=0.01 (Table 3): Fourier-feature PI-DeepONet rel-L2 of s = 8.45e-03 +/- 6.65e-03 vs fully-connected 3.48e-01 +/- 2.34e-01; out-of-distribution test on l=0.2 GRFs: 7.12e-03. Burgers: worst-sample rel-L2 17.10e-02 (standard MLP) reduced to 3.31e-02 (modified MLP, lambda=20); best average errors 2.80e-02 / 1.38e-02. Eikonal circles: rel-L2 = 4.22e-03 over 1,000 test examples
errors_reported: Table 1 (data-driven): s: PI-Tanh 2.49e-03 +/- 2.74e-03, DeepONet-ReLU 5.16e-03 +/- 4.58e-03, DeepONet-Tanh 1.89e-01 +/- 1.51e-01; u: 6.29e-03 +/- 3.65e-03, 1.39e-01 +/- 5.58e-02, 6.14e-01 +/- 2.36e-01. Table 2 (physics-only): s: PI 3.25e-03 +/- 3.19e-03 vs DeepONet 8.80e-01 +/- 4.72e-01; u: 6.97e-03 +/- 3.95e-03 vs 9.15e-01 +/- 1.86e-01. Table 3 (irregular inputs): s: 8.45e-03 +/- 6.65e-03 (Fourier feature) vs 3.48e-01 +/- 2.34e-01 (fully-connected); u: 8.25e-03 +/- 1.54e-03 vs 6.81e-01 +/- 6.31e-02. OOD test (l=0.2 GRF): 7.12e-03. Burgers: avg 2.80e-02 (standard MLP) / 1.38e-02 (modified MLP, lambda=20). Eikonal circles: 4.22e-03
speedup_claims: A trained physics-informed DeepONet predicts the solution of O(10^5) time-dependent PDEs in a fraction of a second - up to three orders of magnitude faster than the conventional spectral solver [55] (single V100; Appendix Fig 14); Burgers inference ~10ms per spatio-temporal solution; inference trivially parallelizable
ablations: (1) Activation: ReLU vs Tanh vanilla DeepONet - both learn inaccurate operators (Fig 2, Table 1); (2) training-set size sweep: vanilla DeepONet needs >10x data to match PI accuracy (Fig 4); (3) FC vs Fourier-feature network on irregular inputs: rel-L2 3.48e-01 -> 8.45e-03 (Table 3); (4) Burgers IC weight lambda in {1,5,10,20,50,100}: best 1.38e-02 at lambda=20 (Fig 11a); (5) modified MLP vs standard MLP backbone (Fig 11a, eqs G.1-G.6); (6) batch size {256,1024,4096,8192,10000}: larger batches improve accuracy, rel-L2 dropping from above 1e-2 to ~3.3e-3 (Fig 24); (7) PI vs vanilla DeepONet training cost (Table 8)
stated_limitations: Section 5 (p.16): optimal feature embedding and network architecture for a given parametric PDE unknown; how to design algorithms that accelerate training and ensure accuracy/robustness of predictions unknown; appropriate weights in the physics-informed loss unknown; multi-scale parametric PDEs may require multi-scale Fourier feature networks (Wang et al. [60]). Section 4.3 (p.13): PI-DeepONet cannot accurately reconstruct the Burgers initial condition (large error near t=0), motivating lambda re-weighting. Section 4.1 (p.9): comprehensive network-architecture study 'beyond the scope of the present study'. Appendix B (p.22): hyper-parameters tuned manually without seeking the absolute best setting
failure_modes: Vanilla DeepONet learns a degenerate operator when trained without paired data (fits only s(0)=0; erroneous predictions for x>0, Fig 6 / Table 2); DeepONet with tanh + paired data still inaccurate (1.89e-01); conventional FC trunk networks cannot capture high-frequency solutions from irregular (l=0.01) inputs; unweighted Burgers loss fails to reconstruct the initial condition; PI training is slower per iteration than data-driven DeepONet due to the autodiff graph (Table 8)
reproducibility: Code and data publicly available: https://github.com/PredictiveIntelligenceLab/Physics-informed-DeepONets; complete hyper-parameter, architecture and cost tables in Appendix B/C (Tables 5-8); all timings on a single NVIDIA V100; random seeds not stated. Analyzed PDF is arXiv:2103.10974v1 (preprint of the Science Advances paper)
quotable_finding: "Strikingly, the proposed framework can be employed to solve parametric PDEs in an unsupervised manner, i.e. without any paired input-output observations." (p.16, Section 5)
relevance_rqs: RQ2 (components): branch/trunk operator architecture + autodiff PDE-residual soft penalty defines physics-informed operator learning; RQ3 (physics+mechanism): residual of G_theta(u)(y) w.r.t. trunk coordinates penalized at Q collocation points per input function - enables operator learning with zero paired input-output data; RQ1 (problem classes): forward parametric PDE surrogates for engineering design/control (airfoil SDF geometry); RQ4 (reliability): explicit limitations, loss-weight sensitivity and batch-size ablations
manuscript_section: S4 methods (physics-informed operator learning: architecture + loss design); T1/T2 (enforcement-mechanism taxonomy: soft-penalty on operator outputs vs data-driven DeepONet); F2 (architecture genealogy: DeepONet descendants); S5 (airfoil geometry / signed-distance-function application)
cross_paper_links: builds-on: PINN-B12 (DeepONet, Lu et al. [33]) and PINN-A01 (PINNs, Raissi et al. [14] - source of the soft-penalty residual idea); compares-to: PINN-B13 (FNO, Li et al. [32] - adopts its Burgers benchmark; claims comparable accuracy with zero paired data); loss-weighting discussion cites PINN-A06 (NTK view of PINN training failures, Wang et al. [61]) and PINN-A07 (self-adaptive soft attention, McClenny & Braga-Neto [62]); modified-MLP backbone from Wang et al. gradient-pathologies paper [57]; also builds on Chen & Chen operator universal approximation [34,35] and random Fourier features [54]
notes_caveats: All evaluation is on synthetic math benchmarks (1D / 1D+time / 2D): no experimental data, no UQ, no seed-replicated error bars; Burgers accuracy vs FNO is only qualitative ('comparable') with no head-to-head numbers, and PI-DeepONet uses N=1,000 training functions vs FNO's large paired corpus; Burgers best mean error (1.38e-02) is orders of magnitude worse than the 1D ODE cases; IC reconstruction weakness openly reported; hyper-parameters hand-tuned; minor paper inconsistencies: airfoil domain called 'unit square' but is [-3,3]x[-3,3], Table 5 lists 500 airfoil test shapes vs 552 in the text; analyzed PDF is the arXiv v1 preprint (33 pp incl. appendices A-H), not the typeset Science Advances version
